title: Lifting fibre sections when first coherent cohomology vanishes
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, and let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $F$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] flat over $S$, meaning that $F_x$ is flat as an $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$-module for every $x\in X$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Fix $s\in S$, let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field], and write $F_s$ for the tensor pullback of $F$ to $X_s$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $H^1(X_s,F_s)=0$ [pqf-def-cohomology], then for every $t\in\Gamma(X_s,F_s)$ there are an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ and a section $\widetilde t\in\Gamma(f^{-1}U,F)$ whose restriction to $X_s$ is $t$.

source.place: Tag 07VK, lemma-perfect-direct-image, canonical derived base change and a finite-free representative; degree-zero section-lifting consequence for a relatively flat invertible sheaf when H^1 of the fibre vanishes. This consequence is agent-extracted, not a verbatim assertion of 07VK.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-section-normalized-stalk-complex] to obtain C over O_(S,s), its finite-free support bounds, the pushforward-stalk comparison e0, and the two fibre comparisons eF0 and eF1 with their section normalization.
Transport the given H^1 vanishing through eF1. Apply [lem-sfb-local-residue-cohomology-lifting] to C. For the class eF0^(-1)(t), surjectivity gives y in H^0(C) reducing to that class.

Represent the germ e0(y) in (f_*F)_s by a section t' on an open U containing s, using Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.exists_germ_eq. Sections of f_*F on U are definitionally sections of F on f^(-1)U. Substitute this germ identity and the chosen reduction identity into the normalized comparison. The inverse identities for e0 and eF0 give exactly the required restriction equality.
